AssemblyScript compiler
=======================

Chrome Preview package only (packaging/package.ts PRUNE_PREVIEW_CHROME).
packaging/verify-store-artifact.ts fails a store artifact that contains it.
Firefox packages omit it because the AMO linter refuses to parse a JavaScript
file over 5 MB (binaryen/index.js). The web target omits it too.

Patch
-----
Browsers resolve bare module names only through an import map, and a Worker
has none. The extension CSP also blocks fetch of a data: URL. Each edit below
is an exact string replacement with an exact count:

  asc.js
    2 x from"binaryen"        ->  from"./binaryen/index.js"
    1 x from"assemblyscript"  ->  from"./assemblyscript.js"
  assemblyscript.js
    2 x from"binaryen"        ->  from"./binaryen/index.js"
    2 x from"long"            ->  from"./long/index.js"
    1 x WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch(cy))
        ->  WebAssembly.instantiate(Uint8Array.from(atob(cy.slice(cy.indexOf(",")+1)),c=>c.charCodeAt(0)))

The last edit decodes the same embedded data: URL (a small f64 pow module)
in memory. No other byte changes.

Audit
-----
The compiler core is an Emscripten build inside binaryen/index.js. It uses no
eval, no Function, no Worker and no SharedArrayBuffer. It needs WebAssembly
under 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. It reads and writes files only through the asc.main
readFile, writeFile and listFiles callbacks. The std library is inside asc.js.
The dynamic import() calls in asc.js and binaryen/index.js run only under
Node. The one browser path is a --transform module, which runs JavaScript.
peerd's Pod asc command refuses --transform and any config file that sets a
transform (engine-tabs/pod-tab/asc-command.js).

Update procedure
----------------
1. Download the three tarballs and check them against the registry
   dist.integrity values.
2. Copy the files listed above.
3. Apply the patch with the same exact counts. Stop if a count differs.
4. Record the new versions and hashes here.
5. Run `bun packaging/check-vendor.ts --write`.
